title: Turbidity & Waterborne Illness
summary: Turbid water harbors suspended microbial pathogens and shields bacteria from natural solar UV disinfection.
action: Avoid direct ingestion or domestic use without certified multi-barrier filtration and boiling.
source: WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality (4th ed.)

title: pH Imbalance & Aquatic Gill Health
summary: Water pH below 6.5 or above 8.5 induces severe mucus secretion on fish gills, impairing gas exchange and juvenile survival.
action: Investigate acidic industrial effluent or agricultural lime runoff upstream immediately.
source: US EPA Aquatic Life Ambient Water Quality Criteria

title: Algae Blooms & Cyanotoxin Livestock Hazard
summary: Nutrient-rich stagnant water spawns cyanobacteria producing microcystin hepatotoxins lethal to drinking cattle and dogs.
action: Fence off stream access for livestock and report immediate green scum layers to agricultural extension officers.
source: FAO Veterinary Public Health & Water Quality Manual

title: Raw Sewage & Enteric Pathogen Outbreaks
summary: Untreated sewage introduces Vibrio cholerae, Salmonella, and rotaviruses directly into downstream community bathing waters.
action: Issue municipal sanitary notices and trace point-source septic bypasses within 500 meters.

title: Water Stagnation & Arboviral Vector Breeding
summary: Blocked stream channels and sluggish flow speeds create optimal oviposition sites for Aedes and Culex mosquito species.
action: Initiate community channel de-silting and remove plastic obstructions to restore natural hydrodynamics.
source: National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP)

title: Plastic Waste & Freshwater Microplastic Ingestion
summary: Degrading synthetic polymers fragment into microfibers that block digestive tracts of native benthic organisms and fish fry.
action: Organize stream cleanup drives with proper solid-waste segregation and barrier netting.
source: UNEP Marine and Freshwater Litter Assessment

title: Sedimentation & Benthic Spawning Smothering
summary: Uncontrolled bank erosion blankets pebble beds with fine silt, eliminating oxygenated microhabitats for mayfly nymphs.
action: Establish vetiver grass and native tree riparian buffers along exposed embankments.
source: Freshwater Biological Association Stream Hydrology Guide

title: Nutrient Overload & Eutrophic Hypoxia
summary: Agricultural fertilizer runoff triggers midnight dissolved oxygen crashes as decaying organic matter consumes oxygen.
action: Encourage precision irrigation and contour planting to reduce overland fertilizer drift.
source: IPBES Global Assessment on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services

title: Heavy Metal Bioaccumulation in Food Chains
summary: Persistent industrial contaminants concentrate in trophic predators, leading to neurotoxic risks in fish-consuming populations.
action: Enforce zero-liquid discharge regulations for upstream plating, tanning, and textile units.
source: Lancet Commission on Pollution and Health

title: Riparian Buffer Degradation & Flash Flood Vulnerability
summary: Loss of natural wetlands and riverbank vegetation accelerates runoff velocity and increases downstream flood severity.
action: Designate community catchment reserves and preserve natural floodplain meanders.
source: UNDRR Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction
